title: BYO corpus record — linear
description: A Linear issue. `team` is the grouping unit, because `data.team.issues` is how both the GraphQL API and the official clients reach issues and because an issue's identifier prefix (ENG-123) IS the team key. Field names are Linear's own — `state` (not status), `estimate`, camelCase `branchName`/`dueDate` — so a corpus written against the real API needs no renaming. `identifier` and `branchName` are derived when omitted. Comments are served through the `Issue.comments` connection.

content.description: The issue's markdown description — served as `Issue.description` and indexed for search.

doc_id.description: Stable id (default: dsid_<sha256(source_type+title+content)>). The served `Issue.id` UUID is derived from it.

team.description: The owning team, e.g. "engineering". Its short key (ENG) is derived from the name and is what identifiers are prefixed with. Default: the source_type.

group.description: ACL group owning the team (default: slug(team)); null means the container owns no group, so nothing is group-scoped to it.

identifier.description: Human identifier, e.g. "ENG-123". Default: synthesized as <TEAMKEY>-<n> from the doc_id. Not required to be unique — the bench's own keys repeat — and `issue(id:)` resolves a repeated identifier to the first matching issue.

parent.description: The parent issue's identifier (e.g. "ENG-20297"), served as `Issue.parent`. Resolved at serve time through the same ACL-scoped lookup `issue(id:)` uses, so a parent the caller cannot read comes back null.

relations.description: Issue relations, served as `Issue.relations` / `inverseRelations`. Each names a target by doc_id; an unresolvable target is a load error, never a dangling relation.

state.description: Workflow state NAME, e.g. "In Progress" / "Done" / "Backlog". Its Linear category (triage|backlog|unstarted|started|completed|canceled) is derived from the name and served as `state.type`.

priority.description: Linear's 0-4 scale (0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low). A label ("Urgent", "High") or a bench-style "P0"-"P3" is accepted and normalized onto that scale.

estimate.description: Complexity estimate in the team's scale.

labels.description: Label names, served through the `labels` connection.

cycle.description: Cycle name, e.g. "2025-W08"; served as `cycle { name }`.

attachments.description: External links on the issue, served as `Issue.attachments`. A bare URL string is accepted; `title` is derived from the last path segment when absent, since Linear declares it non-null.

branchName.description: Suggested git branch. Default: Linear's own derivation, <assignee>/<identifier>-<title slug>.

dueDate.description: Due date as a bare YYYY-MM-DD (Linear's TimelessDate scalar).

assignee.description: Assignee's email. Omit for an unassigned issue — `assignee` then resolves to null, as it does in Linear.

assigneeName.description: Assignee display name (default: derived from the email).

author_name.description: The owner's display name as the corpus writes it, served as the document's owner (a name is not recoverable from an email address).

visibility.description: public = org-wide, group = the team's group, private = creator only.

readers.description: Explicit reader principals. `user:<email>` / `group:<id>` / `org:<name>` state the type; unprefixed, an address is a user and anything else a group. Overrides visibility — and an EMPTY array means nobody may read the document (admin-only), not everybody.

comments.description: Comments on the issue, served through `Issue.comments`.

meta.description: Free-form per-source structured extras merged into the record.

created.description: createdAt (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Default: synthesized from doc_id.

updated.description: updatedAt (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Defaults to createdAt when absent, since Linear declares updatedAt non-null.
